chunkError.message: Part of the app could not be loaded (it was probably updated). Reload to continue.

appError.message: Something went wrong while displaying the app. Reload the page to continue.

language.label: Language
language.description: Applies only to this browser. French is the default.

chat.locationReady: Send the radio GPS as a location pin.

messageList.deleteConfirm: This removes the message from this device. Other mesh nodes still have it.
messageList.noEchoes: No echoes yet — view message status
messageList.analyzeDescription: On-demand raw packet analysis for a message-backed archival packet.
messageList.analyzeNotice: This analyzer shows one stored full packet copy only. When multiple receives have identical payloads, the backend deduplicates them to a single stored packet and appends any additional receive paths onto the message path history instead of storing multiple full packet copies.
messageList.analyzeUnavailable: No archival raw packet is available for this message, so packet analysis cannot be shown.
messageList.analyzePurged: The archival raw packet for this message is no longer available. It may have been purged from Settings > Database, so only the stored message and merged route history remain.
messageList.analyzeLoadFailed: Could not load the archival raw packet for this message: {{description}}
messageList.observerReachCaveat: Nodes that published hearing this message to Meshloom Community:
messageList.observerReachEmpty: No node has published hearing this packet to Meshloom Community.
messageList.observerReachCommunityOff: Who heard this packet comes from Meshloom Community. Turn Community on to see it.
messageList.observerReachMapAria: Map of the nodes that heard this packet

settings.staleHelp: Off by default. When set, a background job deletes non-favorite contacts using the same last-heard-before filter as Bulk Delete. 0 disables the job.
settings.groupsHelp: Local labels for the sidebar. Groups are not synced to the radio.
settings.directoryViaStats: Meshloom Community is on, so hop names, locate, and heard-by counts come from Community. The browser never contacts Community directly; the server relays. 1-byte hops are never sent.
settings.backupKeyWarning: The database download holds no radio private key (Meshloom keeps it in memory only). The full backup includes it, with the radio settings: use it to keep the node's identity across a reflash.
settings.backupDbHelp: Full snapshot of meshcore.db: mesh history, channel keys, VAPID keys, fanout configs (MQTT, webhooks, SQS), extensions without their secrets, and push subscriptions. Treat this file as a secret. It leaves out the radio private key (it lives in memory), account passwords, authenticator secrets and recovery codes, the Bluetooth PIN, and the Meshloom Remote and link-sharing keys. Restore is operator-level: stop the server and replace the file yourself. This app will not overwrite the live database.
settings.backupJsonHelp: Contacts, channels, settings, and groups only. No messages, packets, radio settings or private key: the full backup has those.
settings.restoreJsonHelp: Merges into the live database. Does not replace meshcore.db and does not delete messages, packets, or contacts missing from the file. Reload the page after restore.
settings.restoreConfirm: I understand this merges into the live database
settings.restoreMergedDetail: {{contacts}} contacts, {{channels}} channels, {{groups}} groups. Reload the page.
settings.giphyKeyHelp: Optional. Adds GIFs to the composer's + button. Create a free beta key at developers.giphy.com. Incoming GIFs render without a key (they load from media.giphy.com).

local.deviceOnly: These settings apply only to this device/browser.
local.localLabelHelp: Names this Meshloom across the top of every page, for when you run more than one. Kept with the instance, so it shows from any device. Leave it empty for no band at all.
local.distanceUnitsHelp: Controls how distances are shown throughout the app.
local.reopenLastHelp: Automatically reopen to the last-open channel or contact when the app loads to the bare URL.
local.autoFocusHelp: Place the cursor in the message input when switching conversations. Desktop only.
local.batteryPercentHelp: Display the radio's battery percentage on the radio status badge. Data updates every 60 seconds and may take up to a minute to appear after connecting.
local.batteryVoltageHelp: Display the radio's battery voltage on the radio status badge. Data updates every 60 seconds and may take up to a minute to appear after connecting.
local.statusDotPulseHelp: Flash the connection status dot in color as packets arrive: blue for channel, purple for DM, cyan for advert, green for other.
local.richPayloads: Render MeshCore Open reactions as emoji
local.richPayloadsHelp: MeshCore Open clients send emoji reactions as encoded text (e.g. r:1a2b:05). When enabled, unmatched reaction messages render as the emoji instead of the raw text. GIFs always display as images — they load from media.giphy.com, which reaches outside your local network and exposes your IP to Giphy.
local.pathHopWidthHelp: Append the per-hop identifier width to the hop-count badge on received messages — e.g. (2 · 2B) for a 2-hop path with 2-byte hops. Direct (0-hop) messages show no width.
local.textReplaceHelp: Automatically replace characters as you type in the message input. Define replacements as a JSON object mapping source strings to their replacements.
local.textReplaceUnsaved: {{error}} Changes are not saved until this is resolved.
local.fontSizeHelp: Scales the app's typography for this browser only. The slider moves in 5% steps; the number field accepts any value from 25% to 400%.

preview.intro: Preview alert, message, sidebar, and badge contrast for the selected theme.
preview.connected: Connected preview: radio link healthy and syncing.
preview.infoAlert: Info: channel slot cache refreshed from radio.
preview.errorAlert: Error: post-connect setup timed out. Reboot the radio and restart.

notifications.thisDeviceHelp: Receive notifications even when the browser is closed. Use the bell icon in a conversation header to override that contact or channel, or subscribe this browser to receive the defaults below.
notifications.thisDeviceGlobalHelp: Default rules and conversation exceptions are shared by every subscribed browser on this install. Subscribing or unsubscribing a browser only controls whether that browser receives them.
notifications.unsupported: Push notifications are not supported by this browser.
notifications.needsHttps: Web Push requires HTTPS. Access Meshloom over HTTPS (self-signed certificates work) to enable push notifications.
notifications.devicesHelp: Each account manages its own browsers. A push reaches a browser while the account that subscribed it is enabled and may send.
notifications.otherDevicesHelp: As an administrator you can remove a device of another account (a lost phone, a former member). Only its owner can rename or test it.

mine.title: My notifications
mine.help: Choose which events notify the devices of your account. Each line follows the administrator's default unless you change it. E-mail, webhook and other shared destinations stay with the administrator.
mine.saveFailed: Could not save your notification rules
mine.pauseHelp: Silence the devices of your account for a while. Urgent alerts and the events the administrator marked “always deliver” still arrive. Other accounts and shared destinations are not affected.
mine.conversationsHelp: Silence or always notify for one channel or contact on your devices. It wins over the lines above for that conversation; a muted conversation or a blocked sender still stays silent.

notifications.defaultsHelp: Choose where each event is delivered. First-seen alerts fire after radio setup when a new companion, repeater, or sensor appears on the mesh. Unknown nodes and room servers never trigger a first-seen notification. Telemetry alerts are configured on the Alerts page.
notifications.newContactHelp: Notify when a companion contact is first seen. Either this toggle or Companion advertisements is enough.
notifications.newDmHelp: Notify on incoming direct messages and room-server posts, unless a conversation exception overrides it.
notifications.advertRepeaterHelp: Notify when a repeater is first seen on the mesh.
notifications.advertCompanionHelp: Notify when a companion node is first seen. Either this toggle or New contacts is enough.
notifications.advertSensorHelp: Notify when a sensor is first seen on the mesh.
notifications.channelFoundHelp: Notify when a new hashtag channel is found. Conversation exceptions do not apply.
notifications.telemetryAlertHelp: Notify when a tracked telemetry reading raises an alert. Conversation exceptions do not apply.
notifications.ossUpdateHelp: Notify when a Meshloom update is available for this node.
notifications.exceptionsHelp: Per-conversation overrides set from the chat-header bell menu. Push, email, and webhook are chosen separately for that thread.
notifications.vapidSubjectHelp: VAPID contact: mailto:you@domain.tld (recommended) or https://your-host with no path. Leave it empty to use the Meshloom Remote address while Remote is on, otherwise a built-in address. Apple rejects .local addresses.

vapidSubjectInUse.remote: In use: {{subject}} (the Meshloom Remote address, because the field above is empty).
vapidSubjectInUse.default: In use: {{subject}} (built-in address). iPhones and iPads refuse it: type a contact above, or turn on Meshloom Remote.

notifications.vapidSubjectInvalid: Must be empty, a mailto:you@domain.tld, or an https://host origin (no path).
notifications.destinationsHelp: Reusable email and webhook destinations. Any enabled notification type can use them. Secrets are not shown after save.
notifications.webhookNotFanout: This webhook is for Meshloom notifications. It is not the Fanout message webhook.

alerts.globalRulesHelp: These defaults apply to every polled node unless that node has an override. A threshold is checked only when a poll returns a usable value.
alerts.polledNodesHelp: Tracked repeaters and contacts. Uncheck Alerting to keep polling a node without firing alerts.
alerts.noPolledNodes: No nodes are being polled. Enable tracking from a repeater dashboard or contact info pane.
alerts.overrideHelp: Change enablement or threshold for this node only. Reset restores the global rules.
alerts.latchesHelp: Rules that are still latched on a tracked node. They clear when the reading returns past hysteresis.

battery.label: Battery
battery.help: Alert when reported battery is below this voltage.

noise.label: Noise floor
noise.help: Alert when reported noise floor is above this level.

rssi.label: Last RSSI
rssi.help: Last packet heard by the repeater, not link quality to that node. Alert when RSSI is below this level.

snr.label: Last SNR
snr.help: Last packet heard by the repeater, not link quality to that node. Alert when SNR is below this level.

tx_queue.label: TX queue
tx_queue.help: Alert when the repeater transmit queue is above this length.

silence.label: Missed polls
silence.help: Alert after this many polls with no usable reply. Radio busy is not a miss.

gps_lost.label: GPS lost
gps_lost.help: Alert when a node that previously reported GPS stops including a fix.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.help: Alert on LPP temperature against this threshold.

humidity.label: Humidity
humidity.help: Alert on LPP humidity against this threshold.

barometer.label: Barometer
barometer.help: Alert on LPP barometer against this threshold.

voltage.label: Voltage
voltage.help: Alert on LPP voltage against this threshold.

current.label: Current
current.help: Alert on LPP current against this threshold.

luminosity.label: Luminosity
luminosity.help: Alert on LPP luminosity against this threshold.

altitude.label: Altitude
altitude.help: Alert on LPP altitude against this threshold.

power.label: Power
power.help: Alert on LPP power against this threshold.

distance.label: Distance
distance.help: Alert on LPP distance against this threshold.

energy.label: Energy
energy.help: Alert on LPP energy against this threshold.

direction.label: Direction
direction.help: Alert on LPP direction against this threshold.

concentration.label: Concentration
concentration.help: Alert on LPP concentration against this threshold.

radio.disconnectHelp: Disconnect pauses automatic reconnect attempts so another device can use the radio.
radio.pathHashHelp: Meshloom defaults to 2-byte hops. 1-byte hashing is harder to disambiguate on a busy mesh.
radio.pathHashUnavailable: The radio did not report its path hash mode, so it cannot be changed here and Meshloom could not apply its 2-byte default. Either the firmware is too old to support it, or the radio did not answer while connecting. Reconnect the radio; if this stays, update its firmware.
radio.advertLocationHelp: Companion-radio firmware does not distinguish between saved coordinates and live GPS here. When enabled, adverts include the node's current location state. That may be the last coordinates you set from Meshloom or live GPS coordinates if the node itself is already updating them. To use a connected GPS, turn it on in Firmware settings. With Community on, this setting also decides what Community gets: the exact position when enabled, a position rounded to about 1 km when off.

firmware.title: Firmware settings
firmware.loadFailed: Could not read the firmware settings
firmware.saveFailed: Could not save the firmware setting
firmware.unsupported: This firmware does not report any settings.
firmware.empty: The radio reports no setting. A GPS appears here only if it is connected when the radio starts: power the radio off, plug the GPS in, then power it on.
firmware.gpsHelp: When on, the radio uses the GPS for its position and sets its clock from it.

selfTelemetry.title: Radio sensors
selfTelemetry.intro: What the radio itself reports: battery, temperature when the board has a sensor, GPS position when the GPS is on.
selfTelemetry.loadFailed: Could not read the radio sensors

factoryReset.title: Factory reset
factoryReset.intro: Erases everything on the radio and restores the firmware defaults. Use it to start over or to hand the radio to someone else.
factoryReset.needsRadio: Connect the radio to use this.
factoryReset.confirmLabel: Type the radio name to confirm: {{name}}
factoryReset.sent: The radio is resetting. Meshloom will reconnect by itself and ask you to adopt the new identity. Set the radio parameters again in the Radio tab.

radio.telemetrySharingHelp: Controls what this radio shares when other nodes request its telemetry. “Deny” blocks all requests, “Per-Contact” uses per-contact permission flags on the radio, and “Allow All” shares with any requester.
radio.rebootHelp: Some settings may require a reboot to take effect on some radios.
radio.exportHelp: Export saves the current server config to a JSON file. Import loads a config file, applies it, and reboots the radio.
radio.multiAcksHelp: When enabled, the radio sends one extra direct ACK transmission before the normal ACK for received direct messages. This is a firmware-level receive behavior, not a Meshloom retry setting.
radio.autoResendHelp: When enabled, outgoing channel messages that receive no echo within 2 seconds are automatically resent once (byte-perfect, within the 30-second dedup window). Repeaters that already heard the original will ignore the duplicate. This functionality will NOT create double-sent/duplicate messages.
radio.floodScopeHelp: Tag outgoing messages with a region name (e.g. MyRegion). Repeaters configured for that region can forward the traffic, while repeaters configured to deny other regions may drop it. Leave empty to send unscoped (plain flood). Forcing unscoped when a default scope is configured on the radio requires firmware v12 or newer. Individual channels can override this with their own region or an "always unscoped" setting.
radio.knownRegionsHelp: One region name per line. Incoming region-scoped (TransportFlood/TransportDirect) packets are matched against this list so messages and the packet inspector show a readable region label instead of a raw transport code. Saving a change re-tags existing messages whose original packet is still stored.
radio.discoverRegionsHelp: Asks nearby repeaters which regions they flood, so you can populate the list above. Uses repeaters from your last mesh discovery sweep when available, otherwise your most recently seen repeaters. Only repeaters in direct range answer, and this only reveals flood-allowed regions (not blocked ones).
radio.maxContactsHelp: Configured radio contact capacity. Favorites reload first, then background maintenance refills to about 80% of this value and offloads once occupancy reaches about 95%.
radio.maxContactsWarn: Your radio reports a hardware limit of {{max}} contacts. The effective cap will be limited to what the radio supports.
radio.advertIntervalHelp: How often to automatically advertise presence. Set to 0 to disable. Minimum: 1 hour. Recommended: 24 hours or higher.
radio.sendAdvertHelp: Flood adverts propagate through repeaters. Zero-hop adverts are local-only and use less airtime.
radio.meshDiscoveryHelp: Discover nearby node types that currently respond to mesh discovery requests: repeaters and sensors.
radio.noNodesResponded: No supported nodes responded during the last discovery sweep.
radio.heardHere: Heard here: {{snr}} dB SNR / {{rssi}} dBm RSSI. Remote heard us: {{remote}} dB SNR.
radio.importKeyBody: This config file contains a private key. Importing it will change your radio's identity — your radio will have a new public key and other nodes will see it as a different device. This cannot be undone without the original key.
radio.geoUnsupportedHelp: Your browser does not support geolocation
radio.numericRequired: All numeric fields must have valid values
radio.regionsAlreadyListed: All discovered regions are already listed
radio.regionsAdded_one: Added {{count}} region — review and Save Messaging Settings
radio.regionsAdded_other: Added {{count}} regions — review and Save Messaging Settings
radio.exportWithKey: Export generated with the private key
radio.exportWithoutKey: Export generated without the private key
radio.exportWithoutKeyHelp: The radio firmware did not export its private key
radio.invalidConfigHelp: File must contain name and radio parameters (freq, bw, sf, cr)
radio.importKeyRebooting: Config + private key imported, saving & rebooting...
radio.rebootingReconnectRequested: The radio is rebooting to reset its clock. Meshloom reconnects automatically.
radio.connectionChangeFailed: Failed to change radio connection state
radio.connectionChangeFailedHelp: Check radio connection and try again
radio.checkRegionsHelp: Tests candidate names against packets this node has already stored. Needs no radio and sends nothing. A packet cannot be asked which region it belongs to, but a proposed name can be confirmed against one.
radio.checkExamined_one: {{count}} regional packet in the last {{hours}} h.
radio.checkExamined_other: {{count}} regional packets in the last {{hours}} h.
radio.checkNoRegionalTraffic: No regionally routed packet in the last {{hours}} h, so nothing can be confirmed either way. Try again once the mesh has been busy, or ask the repeaters below.
radio.checkNoMatch: None of the names tried explains that traffic. The region is one nobody here has mentioned; ask the repeaters below, or a local operator.

regionOutcome.contact_add_failed: could not be added to the radio, which usually means its contact list is full

radioApp.trackedRepeatersHelp: Repeaters opted into automatic telemetry collection are polled on a scheduled interval. To limit mesh traffic, the app caps telemetry at 24 checks per day across all tracked repeaters — so fewer tracked repeaters allows shorter intervals, and more tracked repeaters forces longer ones. Up to {{max}} repeaters may be tracked at once ({{used}} / {{max}} slots used).
radioApp.alertRulesHelp: Alerts apply only to tracked nodes. A threshold is checked only when a poll returns a usable value.
radioApp.alertsMoved: Thresholds, voices, and per-node overrides now live on the <alerts>Alerts</alerts> page.
radioApp.batteryVoltsMinHelp: Alert when reported battery is below this voltage.
radioApp.noiseFloorMaxHelp: Alert when reported noise floor is above this level.
radioApp.missesBeforeAlertHelp: Alert after this many polls with no usable reply. This is not a second hour setting.
radioApp.intervalClamped_one: Saved preference is {{preferred}} hour, but the scheduler is using {{effective}} hours because {{tracked}} repeater is tracked. Your preference will be restored if you drop back to a supported count.
radioApp.intervalClamped_other: Saved preference is {{preferred}} hours, but the scheduler is using {{effective}} hours because {{tracked}} repeaters are tracked. Your preference will be restored if you drop back to a supported count.
radioApp.pollRoutedHourlyHelp: When enabled, tracked repeaters with a direct or routed path (not flood) are polled every hour instead of on the scheduled interval above. Flood-only repeaters still follow the normal schedule.
radioApp.nextFloodRun: Next flood run at {{time}} (UTC top of hour).
radioApp.nextRun: Next run at {{time}} (UTC top of hour).
radioApp.nextRoutedRun: Next direct/routed run at {{time}} (UTC top of hour).
radioApp.noRepeatersTracked: No repeaters are being tracked. Enable tracking from a repeater's dashboard.
radioApp.trackedContactsHelp: Non-repeater contacts (companions, rooms, sensors) can also be tracked for periodic LPP telemetry collection (battery, sensors, GPS). Up to 8 contacts may be tracked. The daily check ceiling is shared with tracked repeaters — adding contacts may clamp the interval upward.
radioApp.noContactsTracked: No contacts are being tracked. Enable tracking from a contact's info pane.
radioApp.blockDiscovery: Block Discovery of New Node Types
radioApp.blockDiscoveryHelp: Checked types will be ignored when heard via advertisement. Existing contacts of these types are still updated. This does not affect contacts added manually or via DM.
radioApp.blockedTypesWarn: New {{types}} heard via advertisement will not be added to your contact list.
radioApp.blockedContactsHelp: Blocked contacts are hidden from the sidebar. Blocking only hides messages from the UI — MQTT forwarding and extension responses are not affected. Messages are still stored and will reappear if unblocked.
radioApp.noBlocked: No blocked contacts. Block contacts from their info pane, viewed by clicking their avatar in any channel, or their name within the top status bar with the conversation open.
radioApp.bulkDeleteHelp: Remove multiple contacts or repeaters at once. Useful for cleaning up spam or unwanted nodes. Message history will be preserved.

bulk.title: Bulk Delete Contacts
bulk.selectHelp: Select contacts to delete. Message history will be preserved and accessible if a contact is re-added, but will no longer appear in the sidebar.
bulk.confirmHelp: Review the contacts that will be permanently deleted.
bulk.noMatch: No contacts match the selected filters.
bulk.name: Name
bulk.confirmDelete: I confirm permanent, irrevocable deletion of all listed nodes above, totalling {{summary}}, spanning creation dates from {{minDate}} to {{maxDate}}

database.deleteUndecryptedHelp: Permanently deletes stored raw packets that have not yet been decrypted. These are retained in case you later obtain the correct key — once deleted, these messages can never be recovered.
database.purgeArchivalHelp: Deletes the raw packet bytes behind messages that are already decrypted and visible in chat. This frees space but removes packet-analysis availability for those messages. It does not affect displayed messages or future decryption.
database.autoDecrypt: Auto-decrypt historical DMs when new contact advertises
database.autoDecryptHelp: When enabled, the server will automatically try to decrypt stored DM packets when a new contact sends an advertisement. This may cause brief delays on large packet backlogs.
database.invalidRetentionHelp: Retention days must be at least 1
database.purgeFailed: Failed to purge decrypted raw packets

stats.loading: Loading statistics... this can take a while if you have a lot of stored packets.
stats.pathHashHelp: Parsed stored raw packets from the last 24 hours: {{count}}
stats.noPathData: No path data in the last 24 hours.
stats.regionScopeHelp: How much local traffic uses regional flood scoping. Traffic covers all channel messages heard, including channels you have no key for; senders only counts channels you can decrypt, so the two use different denominators and will not match.
stats.floorNoise: Scoped message count is at or below the estimated false-positive floor ({{floor}}) from corrupt packet captures, so it is not evidence of regional adoption.
stats.floorIncludes: Includes an estimated {{floor}} false positives from corrupt packet captures.
stats.noChannelMessages: No channel messages heard in the last 24 hours.
stats.noNoiseSamples: No noise floor samples collected yet. Samples are collected every minute and retained until server restart.
stats.oneNoiseSample: Only one sample so far ({{dbm}} dBm). More data needed for a chart. Samples are collected every minute and retained until server restart.

community.intro: Meshloom Community is optional and stays off until you join. Enter the IATA code of the nearest airport so this server can publish overheard packets and use the Community directory. Your browser never contacts Community directly: everything goes through this Meshloom server.
community.joinHelp: Join Meshloom Community by saving a 3-letter IATA airport code. Nothing is published until you join.
community.bannerMessage: To use all Meshloom Community features, enter the IATA code of the nearest airport.
community.bannerOptedOut: Meshloom Community is off. Turn it on and enter the IATA code of the nearest airport to use all Community features.

suggest.help: Sends your radio's position, rounded to about 1 km, to Community once, even while Community is off. Community records no code; its access logs keep your IP address and that position.
suggest.none: No code to suggest: your radio has no position. Type the code yourself.
suggest.failed: Suggestions are not available right now. Type the code yourself.
suggest.title: Suggested codes: pick one, or type another.
suggest.both: used by your Community neighbours, and the nearest airport

community.disableHelp: Stopping Meshloom Community stops publish, and also stops the online directory: no hop names, no locate anchors, no heard-by counts.
community.iataHelp: The IATA code is the 3-letter code of the nearest airport (A–Z). It is a coarse region label. Concordance only means it is consistent with your radio position — never a verified location.
community.iataInvalid: IATA must be exactly 3 letters A–Z.
community.noIataPublishOff: No IATA code is saved, so publish stays off.
community.iataChangeCap: IATA change cap reached. Try again later.
community.joinIataChangeCap: Community refused this IATA code: this radio already changed its IATA too often in the last 7 days. Community stays off. Join with your previous code, or try again later.
community.overrideHelp: Confirm this IATA even if it is not consistent with your radio position. This confirmation is not change-capped.
community.concordanceOk: This IATA is consistent with your radio position.
community.concordanceWarn: This IATA is only loosely consistent with your radio position.
community.concordanceMismatch: This IATA is not consistent with your radio position.
community.concordanceUnknown: Cannot compare this IATA with your radio position yet.

waiting.banner: Meshloom Community needs your position to work
waiting.title: Community is waiting for your position
waiting.why: Community places each radio on its map to show where packets are heard. Until your radio has a position, it only tells Community that it is online: no packet is sent, and Live, the directory and the statistics stay off.
waiting.leaveHelp: If you would rather not give a position, you can leave Community.
waiting.positionSaved: Position saved on the radio. It is being sent to Community: the banner goes away in a few seconds.
waiting.positionFailed: Could not save the position on the radio
waiting.settingsNote: Community is waiting for your radio's position: only its online status is sent until you choose one.
waiting.featureOff: This comes from Meshloom Community, which first needs your radio's position.
waiting.liveBanner: Community packets will show once your radio has a position. Your own radio's packets still appear.

optOut.title: Leave Meshloom Community?
optOut.intro: Meshloom asks Community to delete your radio’s position, then stops publishing to Community.
optOut.fullDeletion: To have everything deleted, write to <email>privacy@meshloom.app</email>.
optOut.notConfirmedToast: You left Community, but it did not confirm the deletion
optOut.pendingBody: You left Community, but Community did not confirm that it deleted your radio’s position. Retry when you like: Meshloom never retries on its own.

banned.title: Radio banned from Meshloom Community
banned.body: This radio has been banned from Meshloom Community. It no longer shares its packets, hashtags or position with Community, and the live feed is off. Everything else in Meshloom works as usual. If you think this is a mistake, write to <email>ban@meshloom.app</email>.

about.madeBy: Made with love and open source by <author>Pascal M</author>
about.kofi: This code is free, and ad-free, forever. If you love my work, <kofi>buy me a coffee!</kofi>
about.thanks: With great appreciation to those who have made the tools upon which this is built:
about.updateAvailableHelp: This node is v{{current}}. Latest published release is v{{latest}}.
about.autoUpdateHelp: When a new release is published, Meshloom installs it on this node.

updates.nodeClockHelp: Times follow this node's clock, not this browser.
updates.legacyHelper: Re-run the Meshloom installer on the host to switch to the signed update helper. This install still uses the previous helper, which trusts files the container can write.

settings.directoryOff: Meshloom Community is off, so there is no online directory: no hop names, no locate anchors, no heard-by counts. Your radio keeps working. Enable Community in Settings to turn the directory back on.

share.title: Share
share.invalidUri: Not an official meshcore:// contact or channel URI

repeater.loginDescription: Log in to access repeater dashboard
repeater.rememberPasswordWarning: Passwords are stored unencrypted in local browser storage for this domain. It is highly recommended to login via ACLs after your first successful login; saving the password is not recommended.
repeater.pathDiscoveryTitle: Path Discovery. Send a routed probe and inspect the forward and return paths
repeater.favoriteAddTitle: Add to favorites. Favorite contacts stay loaded on the radio for ACK support.
repeater.favoriteRemoveTitle: Remove from favorites. Favorite contacts stay loaded on the radio for ACK support.
repeater.noLoginAttempt: No server login attempt has been recorded in this view yet.
repeater.loginTimeoutDetail: No confirmation came back from the repeater after the {{method}} login attempt.
repeater.loginRespondedUnconfirmedDetail: The repeater responded, but did not confirm the {{method}} login attempt.
repeater.loginRequestFailedSummary: We couldn't send the login request.
repeater.loginRequestFailedDetail: The repeater never acknowledged the {{method}} login attempt. {{message}}
repeater.name: Name
repeater.mapUnavailable: Map and distance data are unavailable until this repeater has a valid position from either its advert or a Node Info fetch.
repeater.regionsNoteAnon: Guest view: flood-allowed regions only (log in as admin for the full hierarchy)
repeater.regionsTruncated: List truncated by the radio — showing the first regions only
repeater.noRegions: No regions returned. The repeater may be unreachable, or full region details require admin access.
repeater.floodAllowedTitle: Flood is allowed for this region
repeater.floodBlockedTitle: Flood is blocked for this region
repeater.downloadCsvTitle: Download all telemetry history as CSV
repeater.historyHelp: Any time repeater telemetry is fetched, the metrics are stored for 30 days (or 1,000 samples, whichever comes first). This telemetry is stored on normal interactive fetches via the repeater pane, API calls to the endpoint ({{endpoint}}), or when the repeater is opted into interval telemetry polling, in which case the repeater will be polled for metrics automatically. Fetch frequency can be configured in <settings>Settings → Radio-App Management</settings>, where you can also see which repeaters are currently opted in. A maximum of {{max}} repeaters may be opted into this for the sake of keeping mesh congestion reasonable.
repeater.removeTracking: Remove Repeater from Interval Metrics Tracking
repeater.optInTracking: Opt Repeater into Interval Metrics Tracking

contactInfo.title: Contact Info
contactInfo.nameUnknownKey: We have not heard an advertisement associated with this name, so we cannot identify their key.
contactInfo.prefixOnly: We've received a message from this sender but don't have their full identity yet. This contact stays read-only until their identity is confirmed — this usually happens automatically when they next advertise.
contactInfo.unknownFullKey: This sender's profile details (name, location) haven't arrived yet. They will fill in automatically when the sender's next advertisement is heard.
contactInfo.favoriteHelp: Favorite contacts stay loaded on the radio for ACK support
contactInfo.hourlyHelp: Hourly lines compare the last 24 hours against 7-day and all-time averages for the same hour slots.
contactInfo.nameOnlyHelp: Name-only analytics include channel messages only.
contactInfo.attribution: Channel sender identity is based on best-effort name matching. Different nodes using the same name will be attributed to the same {{kind}}. Stats below may be inaccurate.
contactInfo.attributionAlias: Historical counts below may include messages previously attributed under names shown in Also Known As.
contactInfo.noSensorData: No sensor data in last response
contactInfo.discoveryDescription: Send a routed probe to this contact and wait for the round-trip path response. The learned forward route will be saved back onto the contact if a response comes back.
contactInfo.forcedWarning: A forced route override is currently set for this contact. Path discovery will update the learned route data, but it will not replace the forced path. Clearing the forced route afterward is enough to make the newly discovered learned path take effect. You only need to rerun path discovery if you want a fresher route sample.
contactInfo.routingDescription: Set a forced route for this contact. Leave the field blank to clear the override and fall back to the learned route or flood until a new path is heard.
contactInfo.forcedRouteHelp: Use comma-separated 1, 2, or 3 byte hop IDs for an explicit path.
contactInfo.forcedRouteNote: Note: direct messages that do not see an ACK retry up to 3 times. The final retry is sent as flood, even when forced routing is configured.

channelInfo.title: Channel Info
channelInfo.floodDescription: Channel-level regional routing temporarily changes the radio flood scope before send and restores it after. This can noticeably slow channel sends. Choose one of three modes below: scope to a region, force unscoped (plain flood, ignoring your global region), or inherit the global setting.
channelInfo.pathHashDescription: Override the path hash mode for this channel. Wider hop identifiers improve repeater disambiguation but extend send time and will prevent users on old (<1.14) firmware from receiving the message.
channelInfo.radioDefaultHelp: Use the radio-wide path hash mode setting
channelInfo.hop1Help: Least repeater disambiguation, up to 63 hops
channelInfo.hop2Help: Better repeater disambiguation, up to 32 hops
channelInfo.hop3Help: Best repeater disambiguation, up to 21 hops

sensor.title: Sensor telemetry
sensor.historyHelp: Any time sensor telemetry is fetched, the readings are stored for 30 days (or 1,000 samples, whichever comes first). This telemetry is stored on interactive requests here, API calls to the endpoint ({{endpoint}}), or when the contact is opted into interval telemetry polling. Fetch frequency can be configured in <settings>Settings → Radio-App Management</settings>. A maximum of {{max}} contacts may be opted in.
sensor.noHistory: No history yet. Request telemetry above to record data points.
sensor.trackingFullHelp: Disable tracking on another contact to free a slot: {{names}}
